1  JUDGMENT 1. Briefly stated the prosecution case is that all accused persons, namely Arvind (husband of deceased), Satyabir Singh (chacha sasur), Sanjeev Dheer (dewar), Saktumal (father-in- law) and Ramnandi (mother-in-law), in furtherance of their common intention with each other subjected Ms.
Anju (deceased) to cruelty and harassed and coerced her for fulfillment of demands of dowry. It is further the case of the prosecution that on 22nd / 23rd of March, 2011, at House no. 363, Gali no. 6,
Durgapuri Extension, Delhi, Anju (deceased) died by hanging, within seven years of her marriage and soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty and harassment by accused persons and thereby they had caused her 'dowry death' by hanging.
2. The FIR was lodged upon the complaint of complainant Meghraj (father of the deceased), wherein he stated that he had married his daughter with accused Arvind by Hindu rites and culture. After the marriage of his daughter, accused Arvind started demanding dowry from deceased Anju. He alleged that accused Arvind also demanded a car and Rs. 4 lakhs from the complainant/ father of deceased Anju. 
3. On 22.03.2011, a call was received in PS M.S. Park vide DD no. 75B dt. 22.03.2011, and when the police reached at the CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park spot, one lady was found hanging from the celling fan with the help of a chunni. the Crime Team was called at the spot and the photographs of the scene of crime were taken. the body was sent to the mortuary. The concerned SDM / SHD was informed, who recorded the statement of the parents of the deceased on 23.03.2011. The postmortem was conducted on 23.03.2011 and the dead body was handed over to the father of the deceased namely Meghraj. 
4. The FIR No. 58/11, u/s 304B/498A/406/34 IPC was registered vide D.D. entry no. 75 B dated 23.03.2011 and the matter was entrusted to Insp. Rajpal Singh for investigation. Accused Arvind was arrested in the present FIR on 24.03.2011. Thereafter, on 24.04.2011, accused Satyabir Singh was arrested in the present case. 
5. On completion of investigation, the charge-sheet was filed against the accused persons for the offences punishable under sections 498A/304B/406/34 IPC and the case was sent for trial. 
6. Charge was framed upon accused Arvind and Satyabir Singh vide orders dt. 10.08.2011 by the Predecessor of this Court for the offences punishable under section 498A/304B/34 IPC. Further,
separate charge was framed upon accused Sanjeev Dhir vide orders dt. 27.09.2012 by the Predecessor of this Court for the offences punishable under section 498A/304B/302/34 IPC. 
Further, additional charge was framed upon accused Arvind, Satyabir Singh, Saktumal and CNR No.
DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park Ramnandi vide orders dated 13.03.2012 for the offence punishable u/s 302/34 IPC. All the accused persons pleaded not guilty qua their respective charges and claimed trial. 
7. To establish its case, the prosecution had tendered a list of 24 prosecution witnesses in the main chargesheet.

2 8. To prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined 25 witnesses and o1 witness was examined as a Court witness. 
a) The complainant /public witnesses:
9. PW-6 was the mother of the deceased. She deposed that her daughter was married with accused Arvind about four years ago according to Hindu rites and customs. She further deposed that after two months of marriage, her deceased daughter was being harassed and maltreated by her in-laws for the issues of not bringing sufficient dowry. She further deposed that her daughter used to informed regarding the same to her on telephone. She further deposed that from the wedlock, her deceased daughter gave birth to a female child and when PW-6 went to meet her daughter, her in-laws sent her daughter and her minor infant child with PW-6, by stating that they are not capable to look-after her deceased daughter and her child. She further deposed that after one year, accused Saktumal, Arvind and one another person came to her house and they apologized that in future they will not harass or demand anything and upon their assurance, PW-6 had sent her daughter with them. 
CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park 10. She further deposed that after about one month, accused persons again started harassing and maltreating her daughter and demanding four wheeler vehicle and cash of Rs. 4 lakhs. She further deposed that on the day of colour Holi, her deceased daughter informed her through phone call that a quarrel was going on between her and her in-laws. Thereafter, her deceased daughter sent a massage that she was being beaten by her husband, parents in-laws and other family members. She further deposed that she alongwith her husband and three sons went to the matrimonial home of her daughter and found the door of the room closed and one police official was standing outside the door and accused Saktumal, Ramanandi, Satyabir, Sanjeev and Madhuri were also standing outside the door. She further deposed that upon opening the door, they saw that her deceased daughter was hanging with the ceiling fan with the help of chunni. 
11. During cross-examination PW-6 deposed that her daughter had never expressed her willingness about doing any job, but admitted that after her marriage, her daughter had completed her training of one NTT course of one month from her parental house and, from her matrimonial house. She further deposed that on the day of the incident, they had only received a message (SMS), but on that day, her daughter had not spoken to her or anyone in her family. She further deposed that her daughter had remained with her for about one year after the birth of her child and in between, she visited her matrimonial home twice or thrice. She also deposed that on all such CNR No.
DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park occasions, her father-in-law used to take her to her matrimonial home. She further deposed that on one occasion, she remained at her matrimonial home for about 06 months, during which period she was forced to serve her in-laws. 
12. She further deposed that accused Arvind was not happy with her daughter, but her daughter was happy, and for the this reason, her daughter continued residing with him. She further deposed that her daughter told her that her husband was not sleeping and eating with her, and vol. stated that State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
3 both husband and wife never took food together. She also deposed that after the delivery of child,
she had visited the hospital with her daughter-in-law, to see her daughter and her new born child. 
She also deposed that after 3-4 days of said delivery, PW-6 alongwith her husband went to the matrimonial house of her daughter Anju, and on that occasion accused Ramnandi and Saktumal told them to take Anju and her new born daughter in their home. PW-6 denied other formal suggestions put to her regarding incriminating facts. 
13. PW-6 was also confronted with her statement given to police Ex. PW6/DA, as she had stated several new facts in her examination-in-chief, and PW-6 admitted that she had not stated those facts to the police.
14. PW-8 was the father of the deceased. He deposed that her daughter was married with accused Arvind on 02.03.2008, according to Hindu rites and customs. he further deposed that after the marriage her daughter was residing with her husband CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No.
58/11 PS M.S.Park in a joint family. He further deposed that his daughter was blessed with one female child after her marriage. He further deposed that after marriage his deceased daughter was harassed for demands of a four wheeler vehicle and Rs. 4 lakhs. He further deposed that whenever the accused persons used to visit his house, they used to again demand a four wheeler and Rs. 4 lakhs. He further deposed that accused Saktumal (father-in-law of his daughter), used to say 'ya to paisa do nahi to ...... mere sambandh sabhi MLAs aur bade bade netao se hai, aap mera kuch nahi bigad sakte'. He further deposed that some days prior to the day of Holi in the year 2011, he and his wife visited the matrimonial house of his daughter and accused Arvind, his parents, his uncle Satyabir, his brother Sanjeev, and brother of Sanjeev namely Madhuri, all present there and they all demanded Rs. 4 lakhs cash and four wheeler vehicle from them. He further deposed that accused Sanjeev told them that if they do not fulfill the said demand, its consequences would be dangerous. 
He further deposed that accused Satyabir told his brother Saktumal that if PW-8 do not satisfy their demands, they would either leave his daughter or kill her. 
15. He further deposed that on 22.03.2011 at about 11.00 pm, a massage came on the mobile phone of his son and in the said SMS his daughter wrote 'mera pati Arvind, sass sasur aur sara parivar mil kar maar rahe hai aur meri maut ke jimmedar yeh sabhi hain', and his son had shown the said message to him. He further deposed that, thereafter, his son called his daughter and voice of crying of his daughter was CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park coming. He further deposed that he, his wife and his son reached to the house of his daughter at about 12.00 midnight. 
He further deposed that outside the room of his daughter, Arvind, his parents, brother Sanjeev and bhabhi Madhuri, uncle Satyabir and one police official were found standing and the door was closed. 
He further deposed that when his son pushed the door slightly, it opened and after entering into the room, he, his wife and his son saw that the feet of his daughter were touching the bed and she was hanging after tying the chunni around her neck with the ceiling fan. He further deposed that broken pieces of bangles, buttons of shirt, mangalsutra and other articles were found scattered there. He further deposed that from the prevailing scene, it was appearing that his daughter was killed with a pre-plan. He further deposed that police reached at the spot and all the accused persons ran away from there. He further deposed that police collected the scattered articles and took the same into their possession. He further deposed that police removed the hanging dead body from ceiling fan State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
4 and took the same to the hospital. 
16. He further deposed that on next day i.e. 23.03.2011 at about 11:00 am, they went to the office of SDM at Seema Puri and his statement was recorded by the SDM vide Ex.PW8/A. He further deposed that his statement was also recorded by the police at PS. He further stated that on 23.03.2011, the dead body of his daughter was handed over to him after postmortem and after establishing its identification vide Ex. PW8/B. CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park 17. He further deposed that on 07.04.2011, he moved an application to the SDM for safe custody of jewellery of his deceased daughter, which was in her almirah. He further deposed that on 07.04.2011, he was called by the police and he went to the matrimonial house of his deceased daughter where police official met him and police seized the dowry articles vide Ex. PW8/C and Ex.
PW8/D. He further deposed that he handed over the list of dowry articles, photographs of marriage and bills of dowry articles and jewellery to the police. He further deposed that site plan was also prepared by the police. 
18. PW-8 was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State on certain material points which he had not deposed. He admitted that on 24.03.2011, when accused Arvind was arrested at his instance and his son's instance, he was wearing shirt having broken button and during interrogation, he had disclosed that the button of his shirt had broken on the day of incident, when a quarrel / scuffle had taken place between him and his wife. He further admitted that the said shirt was removed from his body by the police and was sealed in a cloth parcel and was taken into possession. He admitted that before concerned SDM, he had stated that due to non fulfillment of the illegal demands of dowry, his son-in-law (accused Arvind) did not use to sleep with his daughter and voluntarily stated that this fact was told to him by his wife. PW-8 also correctly identify the shirt of accused Arvind with two front buttons broken, as Ex. P1.
CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park 19. During cross-examination of PW-8 by Ld. Defence Counsels for the accused persons , he was confronted with his statement Ex. PW8/A, and he admitted that several facts which he had deposed before the Court, were not stated by him to the said SDM. He also stated that he had stated those facts to the police, but the same were also not found in his statement recorded by the police recorded Ex. PW8/DA. He denied in his cross-examination that his daughter was kept at his house for about six months after her marriage, on the pretext that she was undergoing Nursery Teacher Training (NTT). He also stated that at the time of delivery of female child to his daughter, the charges / expenses incurred in the delivery were borne by her in-laws. He admitted that accused Arvind used to run a medical store in a ranted premises after his marriage and further admitted that generally medical stores remain open in Delhi for all seven days and till late hours. He also admitted that the sisters-in-law of his daughter had already been married prior to the marriage of his daughter in the matrimonial home, and also admitted that the mother-in-law of his daughter was suffering from back pain for last five years. He also admitted that there was no female member in the matrimonial home of his daughter for looking after his daughter and her new born child. He State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
5 further deposed that his daughter was brought to her parental home after the delivery of her child,
and she stayed in her parental home for about 6 months thereafter. 
20. PW-8 also admitted in his cross-examination that prior to the death of his daughter, accused Saktumal had already partitioned his house and further admitted that accused CNR No.
DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park Sanjeev was residing in separate portion of the house with his family. He also admitted that at the time of the incident, his daughter was residing on the left portion at the first floor of the house. PW-8 also admitted about an incident which happened in end of December, 2010 and the beginning of January, 2011, when her daughter was brought back from his house by accused Arvind, his father accused Saktumal and one another person. He admitted that on that day, he sent his daughter with the said persons after they agreed that accused Arvind would close his medical store before 09.00 pm and would return to his house in time and would take meals with his daughter. 
21. PW-8 further deposed in his cross-examination that he had informed the concerned SDM that at around 11:00 pm, his son had received an SMS from his daughter, wherein his daughter has alleged that her husband, parents-in-law and their entire family are giving beatings to her and in the same message, it was also written that these persons would be responsible for the death of his daughter.
He also stated that he had shown the message to the concerned SDM and had also given pictures of the said message to the police. The said messages on the judicial file is mark as Mark A and Mark B.
PW-8 admitted that no mobile number is reflected in the said messages. 
22. PW-8 further deposed that accused Sanjeev had got married after about 5-6 months of the marriage of his daughter with accused Arvind. He further deposed that he was not aware as to who had taken the minor daughter of his daughter after the incident. He also stated that he had given the mobile phone CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park in which the message was received, to the police. He also admitted that he had not lodged any complaint against the accused persons with regard to any demand or threat at any point of time, till the death of his daughter. He also admitted that there had been no complaint given by him or his family or his deceased daughter against accused Satyabir Singh and his family members regarding harassment or dowry demand. PW- 8 denied that since accused Arvind did not return home on time, due to this reason, his daughter committed suicide in passion. PW-8 denied all other pre incriminating suggestions put to him by respective denfence counsel. 
23. PW-10 was the brother of deceased. He deposed that his sister got married with accused Arvind on 02.03.2018 according to Hindu rites and customs. He further deposed that in the marriage, they had given the dowry articles as per their capacity and as demanded. He further deposed that after 1-2 months from the marriage, the in-laws of his sister started harassing her by saying 'aap kangle ghar se aayi ho aur hamari maang ke mutabik nahi laayi ho'. He further deposed that whenever his parents used to visit the matrimonial home of his sister, her in-laws used to demand cash amount of Rs. 4 lakhs and four wheeler vehicle. He further deposed that his sister used to inform him about these facts that her husband, her in-laws and her dewar used to harass and maltreat her on account of not fulfilling their demands. 
State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
6 24. He further deposed that on 22.03.2011 at about 11:00 pm, he received a massage from the mobile number of his sister in CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park which she wrote 'meri maut ke jimmedar mera pati, mere saas sasur aur mera pura parivar hai'. He further deposed that after receiving the message, he made a call to his sister on her mobile phone and when the phone was received by his sister, he heard that his sister was weeping and saying while weeping that 'yeh sab log mujhe mil kar maar rahe hain'. He further deposed that he alongwith his parents and his two brothers reached at the house of his sister and found that all the family members i.e.
Arvind, Sanjeev, Ramnandi, Saktumal Dhir, Satyabir were standing outside the door of the room alongwith police official and the door of the room was closed at that time. He further deposed that he slightly pushed the door and it opened and after entering into the room, he found broken pieces of bangles, mangalsutra in broken condition, were lying scattered on the floor in the room. He further deposed that he found his sister was hanging with the ceiling fan and a chunni was tied around her neck and her feet were touching against the mattress of the bed. He further deposed that other police officials also reached there and the accused persons had fled away from there. 
25. He further deposed that next day, they went to the PS and they were asked to reach the hospital.
He further deposed that after postmortem, the dead body was handed over to them after they had identified the dead body of his deceased sister in the hospital. 
26. He further deposed that on 24.03.2011, he joined the investigation with the police and pointed out towards accused CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park Arvind and accused Arvind was arrested vide memo Ex. PW9/A.
27. PW-10 was asked certain leading questions by Ld. APP for the State, wherein he admitted that whenever accused Arvind used to visit their house, he used to demand a four-wheeler vehicle and cash amount of Rs. 4 lakhs and when the said demand was not fulfill, he is refused to sleep with the deceased , and used to taunt her by saying "tum kangle ghar se aayi ho". He further admitted that whenever his sister used to visit their house, she used to complaint that her dewer, dewrani, also used to give beatings to her for not fulfilling the demands of dowry. PW-10 also admitted that at the time of arrest of accused Arvind, he was wearing a shirt with broken buttons and the said shirt was removed from his body and was sealed in a parcel and taken into possession vide seizure memo already Ex. PW9 / C. PW-10 also correctly identified the shirt as Ex. P1.
28. PW-10 was then cross examined by respective Defence Counsels for the accused persons. During cross-examination, PW-10 was confronted with his statement given to the police Ex. PW10/DA, but several facts which he had disclosed before the Court, were not found in the said statement. He specifically denied the suggestion that in March, 2010, he, alongwith his father, brother, one police man namely Brahmpal, and one more person namely Brahmpal who used to work in DTC, went to the matrimonial house of his sister and gave beatings to accused Arvind or that any police call was made at 100 CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park number on that day and when the police arrived, the matter was compromised between them and accused Arvind and his family. He denied that any false allegations were levelled upon accused Arvind casting aspersions on his character, or that in the said night they had brought deceased Anju to their parental home. 
PW-10 also stated that he had given the photographs of the SMS to the police. 
State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
7 29. During cross examination PW-10 also explained that when he mentioned that his sister was living in 'sanyukt parivar' (Joint Family), he meant that accused Arvind, Sanjeev, parents of Arvind namely Saktumal and Ramanandi, were living jointly and cooking food in the common kitchen. He also clarified that after the marriage of accused Sanjeev, his wife also became part of the said joint family. PW-10 admitted that no complaint was made either by him or by his family members against accused Satyabir for taunting his deceased sister, or for harassing her for demands of dowry. PW-10 also deposed that his sister was using mobile phone even prior to her marriage, and that he had purchased the said mobile phone of her sister and he had also given his ID proofs at the time of purchasing SIM for her sister. PW-10 was also confronted with several suggestions, but they are not material. 
30. On 19.09.2023, PW-10 was again recalled by the prosecution u/s 311 Cr.P.C. PW-10 gave a certificate u/s 65B Indian Evidence Act dt. 19.09.2023, Ex. PW10/X, in support of photographs Mark A and Mark B. He also identified one mobile phone produced by MHC(M) in an unseal condition, CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park make Samsung, black and blue colour, which PW-10 identified as the mobile phone of his deceased sister. PW-10 was than cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel, wherein he denied the suggestion that he had filed fabricated certificate Ex. PW10/X.
31. PW-11 was another brother of deceased. He deposed that his sister was got married with accused Arvind on 02.03.2008 according to Hindu rites and customs. He further deposed that at the time of marriage of his sister, accused Arvind was residing in a joint family. He further deposed that his sister was blessed with a female child from the said wedlock. He further deposed that after marriage,
his sister was harassed by accused Arvind, his brother accused Sanjeev, Sanjeev's wife Madhuri, his father accused Saktumal Dhir, his mother accused Ramanandi and uncle of Arvind namely accused Satyabir, on demands of cash amount of Rs.4 lakhs and four wheeler vehicle.
32. He further deposed that on 22.03.2011, his sister sent a message at about 11.00 pm on the mobile phone of his younger brother Pankaj and she wrote in the said SMS 'meri maut ke jimmedar mera pati, saas sasur aur inka poora parivar hai'. He further deposed that after receiving the said message, his younger brother made a call to his sister and his sister told him on the phone that 'ye sab mujhe milkar maar rahe hai'. He further deposed that the voice of screaming of his sister were audible on the phone. He further deposed that, thereafter, he alongwith his father, his elder brother Anil and his younger CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park brother Pankaj,
reached at the matrimonial home of his sister at about 12.30 am and on reaching there, they found that one policeman alongwith accused Arvind, Sanjeev, his parents, his bhabhi Madhuri and uncle Satyabir was standing outside the door of the room of his sister. He further deposed that his younger brother slightly pushed the door of the room and it opened. He further deposed that they entered into the room and saw that his sister was hanging with the ceiling fan with the help of chunni. He further deposed that they noticed that the feet of his sister were touching the bed. He further deposed that bangle pieces, mangal-sutra in broken condition and button of the shirt were found lying. He further deposed that dead body was removed from there. He further deposed that accused persons had ran away when the PCR and local police reached there. PW-11 was also put certain leading questions by Ld. APP for the State, wherein he admitted that accused Arvind used to raise State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
8 demands of cash amount of Rs. 4 lakhs and a four-wheeler vehicle whenever he used to visit their house, and he also refused to sleep with the deceased when the said demands were not fulfilled. 
33. PW-11 was then cross examined at length by respective Defence Counsels for the accused persons. During cross- examination, PW-11 denied all the formal suggestions regarding incriminating facts, and there are no material contradictions. 
34. PW-12 was the uncle of the deceased. He deposed on the same lines as PW-6, PW-8, PW-10 and PW-11. He further CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park deposed that once or twice, he had visited the matrimonial house of his niece Anju as she made the call to them about the quarrels in her house. He further deposed that his niece used to make calls to them and stated that her husband and in-laws used to give beatings to her and also used to raise demand for more dowry articles. He further deposed that when he visited the matrimonial house of Anju second time, dewar of Anju told them 'iske bache hamain hi palne parainge' and thereafter they brought Anju back to her parental house. He further deposed that later, upon assurance of relatives of accused Arvind,
they sent Anju with them. He further deposed that they again committed maar pitai with Anju and a message was received by his nephew on his mobile phone where she wrote that 'mero ko maar peet rahe hain'. He further deposed that after receiving the above said message, he alongwith his brother went to the house of Arvind, where his brother-in-law (father of Anju), his nephew and his sister were already present, and PW-12 witnessed that his niece was hanging in her room and her bangles were lying scattered there in broken condition, and a shirt button was also found there and her mangal-sutra was lying there in broken condition. He further deposed that feet of his niece were touching the bed. He further deposed that accused persons had already fled away from the spot. 
35. PW-12 was then cross examined at length by respective Defence Counsels for the accused persons. During cross- examination, PW-12 denied all the formal suggestions regarding incriminating facts, and there are no material CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park contradictions.
36. PW-13 was the brother of the deceased. He deposed on the same lines as PW-6, PW-8, PW-10,
PW-11 and PW-12.
37. PW-13 was then cross examined at length by respective Defence Counsels for the accused persons. During cross- examination, PW-13 denied all the formal suggestions regarding incriminating facts, and there are no material contradictions. 
b) Police Witnesses and Formal Witnesses :
38. PW-1 W/HC Vandana was the Duty Officer. She deposed that Insp. Ashok Sharma, SHO of M.S.
Park handed over to her one rukka with the direction to register the case u/s 304B/498A/34 IPC,
and she proved the FIR Ex. PW1/A and also proved the endorsement on the rukka vide Ex. PW1/B. 
She was not cross-examined despite opportunity given to the defence.

9 39. PW-2 Ct. Neeraj was the photographer of Mobile Crime Team. He proved the 10 photographs of the spot taken from different angles, the negatives of which are Ex. PW2/A1 to A10 and photographs are Ex. PW1/B1 to B10. He was cross- examined by respective Ld. Defence Counsels for the accused persons, but there are no material contradictions. 
40. PW-3 Ct. Pradeep Kumar was the DD Writer, who CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No.
58/11 PS M.S.Park deposed that on 23.03.2011 at about 12.25 am (midnight), SI Puneet Bharti informed him over telephone regarding a brawl and one lady hanging herself at House no. 363, Gali no. 6, Durga Puri Extension. He proved the said DD entry vide DD no. 75B, Ex. PW3/A. He was cross-examined by respective Ld. Defence Counsels for the accused persons, but there are no material contradictions.

The family members of the deceased have duly corroborated about the said demands and lastly the demand was raised to them when they had visited the matrimonial home of their daughter a day or two before the festival of Holi.

The onus was upon the defence to rebut the said presumption that deceased had not died due to any demands of dowry or any cruelty or harassment in connection with the demands of dowry and also to further rebut the fact that soon before the death of the deceased, no such demands were raised and no such cruelty was committed upon her. Moreover, the prosecution witnesses have also deposed specifically that even accused Satyabir used to raise demands of dowry from the family of the deceased in the same CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park manner as the other accused persons. It has also come on the record that many a times when the family of the deceased used to visit her matrimonial home, accused Satyabir used to be present there. It has also come on the record that accused Satyabir even used to visit the parental home of the deceased with her husband accused Arvind. There is no contrary evidence led on behalf of accused Satyabir to the said facts proved through the testimony of prosecution witnesses. 
141. Accused Sanjeev, who is the brother-in-law (dewar) of the deceased also raised a similar defence that he used to reside in separate portion which had been handed over to him through a register sale deed executed by his deceased mother i.e. accused Ramnandi. He examined DW-2 in support of the said fact, and the copy of the sale deed was filed as Mark A. In order to succeed in charge under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, the prosecution is required to prove that the accused had subjected the deceased to cruelty, as defined in the explanation to the section.

For this purpose, the provision of Sec. 498A IPC is reproduce as under:-
"Sec. 498A IPC. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty:
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty means"--
(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

89. It is clear from a bare reading of the said provision in conjunction with the 'Explanation'
appended to the said section, that it is not every cruelty which is punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

The cruelty, so as to attract penal provisions, contained in Section 498A of Indian Penal Code, has necessarily to be a willful conduct, which is of such a nature that it is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or cause grievous injury or danger to her life or health.

The use of the expression "willful" in the explanation to Section 498A of Indian Penal Code indicates that the conduct attributed to the accused, in order to be culpable, needs to be deliberate, aimed at causing injury to the health of the woman or bringing misery to her.

If the accused knows or is reasonably expected to know that his conduct is likely to cause injury to the life, limb or health of the aggrieved woman or if his conduct is of such a nature, that causing injury to the life, limb or health can be a natural consequence for the woman, who is recipient of such a conduct, it will attract criminal liability on the part of the husband or his relative, as the case may be.

90. It is easily believed that everyone is presumed to intend the natural consequences of his act and such a presumption must necessarily be drawn even if there is no intention to cause any injury or harm to the woman.

Whether the conduct in question is likely to drive the woman to cause injury to her life, limb or health, will depend upon a number of factors such as social and economic status of the parties, the level of awareness of the aggrieved woman, her temperament, state of her health,
physical as well as mental and how she is likely to perceive such a behavior.

If a woman is harassed with a view to coerce her or any of her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security, it will also constitute cruelty, as defined in the explanation to Section 498A of State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/
20 Indian Penal Code.
91. The expression "Cruelty" takes in its ambit mental cruelty CNR No. DLNE01-000072-2011 FIR No. 58/11 PS M.S.Park as well as physical torture of the woman.

If the conduct of the accused with a woman is likely to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that her living with the husband will be harmful and injurious to her life and safety, such a conduct would attract criminal liability,
envisaged in Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

92. If the woman has been harassed on account of her failure or the failure of her relatives to meet an unlawful demand for property or valuable security, that also constitutes cruelty, within the meaning of Section 498A of IPC.

The expression "harassment" has not been defined in Section 498A of IPC, but its dictionary meaning is 'to subject someone to continuous vexatious attacks, questions,
demands or other unpleasantness, etc'.
However, it is not harassment of every nature which is punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
In order to attract criminal liability, there should be torture physical or mental, by positive acts.

Such acts should be aimed at persuading or compelling the woman or her relatives to meet an unlawful demand of any property or valuable security or it should be actuated by the failure of the woman or her relative to meet such a demand.

89. It is clear from a bare reading of the said provision in conjunction with the 'Explanation'
appended to the said section, that it is not every cruelty which is punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
The cruelty, so as to attract penal provisions, contained in Section 498A of Indian Penal Code, has necessarily to be a willful conduct, which is of such a nature that it is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or cause grievous injury or danger to her life or health.
The use of the expression "willful" in the explanation to Section 498A of Indian Penal Code indicates that the conduct attributed to the accused, in order to be culpable, needs to be deliberate, aimed at causing injury to the health of the woman or bringing misery to her.
If the accused knows or is reasonably expected to know that his conduct is likely to cause injury to the life, limb or health of the aggrieved woman or if his conduct is of such a nature, that causing injury to the life, limb or health can be a natural consequence for the woman, who is recipient of such a conduct, it will attract criminal liability on the part of the husband or his relative, as the case may be.
90. It is easily believed that everyone is presumed to intend the natural consequences of his act and such a presumption must necessarily be drawn even if there is no intention to cause any injury or harm to the woman.
Whether the conduct in question is likely to drive the woman to cause injury to her life, limb or health, will depend upon a number of factors such as social and economic status of the parties, the level of awareness of the aggrieved woman, her temperament, state of her health,
physical as well as mental and how she is likely to perceive such a behavior.
If a woman is harassed with a view to coerce her or any of her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security, it will also constitute cruelty, as defined in the explanation to Section 498A of State vs Arvind on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12733997/

If the conduct of the accused with a woman is likely to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that her living with the husband will be harmful and injurious to her life and safety, such a conduct would attract criminal liability,
envisaged in Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

The expression "harassment" has not been defined in Section 498A of IPC, but its dictionary meaning is 'to subject someone to continuous vexatious attacks, questions,
demands or other unpleasantness, etc'.
However, it is not harassment of every nature which is punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
In order to attract criminal liability, there should be torture physical or mental, by positive acts.
